verdict.rationale: Raygun's own docs claim deployment tracking can "identify any new errors or regressions" (raygun-docs-31), and errors can be marked 'Resolved' once fixed (raygun-docs-10). That gives a first-party basis for regression detection tied to releases. However, nothing shows that a resolved error recurring in a newer version triggers its own alert, separate from new-error notifications. missing for 10: documented reactivation of resolved errors in a newer release, a regression-specific alert or notification rule distinct from new-issue alerts, version-aware 'resolved in version X' semantics, independent or hands-on corroboration.
